mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following a GDP increase, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate signals economic weakness, which leads to lower consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to lower corporate earnings and investor pessimism, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates a strong demand for new homes, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST increases > 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment and falling payroll employment signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS declines > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of instances when both conditions are met, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high inflation rate coupled with a rising federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when both conditions are met, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS increases > 2%, this hypothesis is rejected.
